title: I Ran Every Day for 30 Days (as a Total Beginner)
creator: Jules Moves
description:
Thirty days, no rest days, never ran more than a 5k before this. Here's what happened to my legs, my sleep and my mood.

Week 1: 0:00
Week 2: 1:40
Week 3: 2:55
Week 4 and the final run: 4:10

sentences.t: Okay, it's day one, and the plan is very simple, I'm going to run every day for thirty days.
Some background, I am not a runner, the most I've ever done is a 5k, and I walked part of it.
So the rule is at least two kilometers a day, no exceptions, and I'm allowed to go as slow as I want.
Let's go.
Okay, that was two point one kilometers and my lungs are on fire.
Day three, everything hurts, specifically my calves, they feel like rocks.
I read that this is totally normal in the first week, your muscles just aren't used to the impact yet.
So I'm going extra slow today, like conversational pace, which for me is basically a fast walk.
Day five, and something weird is happening, I actually wanted to go out today.
I'm not saying I'm enjoying it, but there's a little part of me that was looking forward to it.
Week two, and the big change is my sleep.
I'm falling asleep way faster, like, I'm out by ten thirty, which never happens.
People keep asking about my shoes in the comments, and honestly there's nothing fancy going on.
They're a pair of Brooks Ghosts that I bought for walking like two years ago, they're pretty beat up.
Someone at my gym said I should get properly fitted at some point, which, fair, I probably will after this.
Day ten, first rainy run.
I almost skipped it, I was standing at the door for like five minutes negotiating with myself.
But it was actually kind of amazing, there was nobody out, the streets were empty, it felt like a movie.
Day fourteen, halfway there, and I did three kilometers without stopping for the first time.
I'm a little emotional about it, I'm not going to lie.
Week three is where it got hard again, mentally, not physically.
The novelty wore off, and it just became a thing I had to do, like brushing my teeth but sweatier.
I had one day where I genuinely did not want to, I'd had a terrible day at work.
And I went anyway, slowly, and I came back in a much better mood, which I guess is the whole point.
My knees started complaining around day eighteen, so I took the advice from you guys and switched to the park trail.
Softer ground, and it made a huge difference within like two days.
Day twenty two, I'm noticing my resting heart rate on my watch has dropped by about six beats.
Which is apparently a real sign your heart's getting more efficient, which is kind of cool to see in numbers.
Okay, it's day thirty.
For the last run I wanted to try a full five kilometers without stopping, the thing I couldn't do a month ago.
Here we go.
Thirty four minutes, which is not fast, but I did not walk once.
So, what changed in thirty days?
My sleep is better, my mood is noticeably better, and I can run five k, which feels ridiculous to say.
What didn't change, honestly, my weight, basically the same, which surprised me but I've read that's pretty normal.
If you're thinking of doing this, go slower than you think, and take the knee pain seriously.
I'm going to keep going, but I'm adding rest days, because my body is asking very politely.
See you on the next one.
